There’s something profoundly humbling about looking up at the night sky and realizing that, no matter how immense our individual ambitions or anxieties feel, they are practically negligible on the cosmic stage. I often find that when life seems vast and complicated—when deadlines loom or relationships grow tangled—a glimpse of a star-strewn sky can restore my sense of perspective. Even though we might be specks of dust in this grand cosmic tapestry, we’re also lucky enough to be a part of it.

I like to imagine if there were people on some distant exoplanet doing exactly what we do—pondering their place in the universe, telling stories, studying science, creating art. Perhaps they’ve broken mysteries we haven’t even dreamed of yet, or maybe they’re just beginning to harness language. It’s both exhilarating and comforting to entertain the idea that we’re not alone in our curiosity.

On Earth, too, there are wonders that rival the cosmos if we look closely. A garden teems with hidden life—tiny ants busily forging pathways, fungi weaving invisible networks beneath the soil, a whole ecosystem choreographed by sunlight and seasons. Dive into the ocean, and you’ll discover realms that look more alien than anything conjured up in fiction—eerie bioluminescent creatures, towering coral cities, vast underwater caverns.

Ultimately, the human experience is a balancing act between exploring the vastness outside and looking inward—caring for our internal universe of thoughts, dreams, and emotions. We may be small, but each life story is important because of how we shape our own pocket of existence. Our capacity for kindness, creativity, and collaboration might well be our most remarkable feature.

So, as we zip through space at astonishing speeds, tethered by gravity to a small but vivid planet, we have the chance to make meaning: to learn, to express love, to protect living wonders around us, and to nurture that curious spark that keeps us looking upward, beyond our confines, to all that remains just out of reach. If the universe is indeed infinite, then there’s an endless horizon of possibility awaiting. And that’s something worth celebrating.
